subject: Post-demo: Clarify prompt/output PII retention and logging
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@helixai.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + quick asks on prompt/output PII retention

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap + two asks so we can move toward the security review: 

1) Recap (features we covered):
- Streaming responses + function call integration
- Model pinning / rollout controls for predictable quality
- Prefix caching / KV cache to reduce token costs
- Audit logs and per-request metadata in the Console

2) Two clarifying asks from your security team:
A) What prompt input and model output (generated tokens) does Redwood persist by default?
B) Where are those artifacts stored (region/residency) and what are the default retention windows?

Attached is a short PDF summary of our default retention & logging and the SOC2 checklist you requested. I captured what I believe we said on the call below, but want to confirm in writing so your legal/security folks have something to review.

What I told you on the call (high-level):
- By default our hosted API does not use customer prompts to train models.
- We persist short-lived request metadata and token-level audit logs for troubleshooting and billing; customers can request longer export windows via dedicated or private deployments.
- Default log retention: 90 days for request traces; 30 days for raw prompt/output payloads (for telemetry / debugging), unless the customer opts into longer retention via contract.
- Data residency: hosted regions in US and EU; residency guarantees via Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated capacity.

Can you confirm whether the HelixAI security team needs us to: (a) redact prompt contents automatically, (b) push logs to your S3/KMS, or (c) keep retention shorter than our defaults? If you can loop in legal or secops on reply that helps.

Thanks — I’ll follow up Monday with a formal copy of the notes for your review.

Best,

Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@helixai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 17:31:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick asks on prompt/output PII retention

Thanks, Olga — appreciated the demo and the clear recap. I looped in our security lead and legal; answering here so we keep a single thread. 

High-level asks from HelixAI security:
- We need a precise list of fields considered PII if present in prompts/outputs (names, SSNs, phone numbers, email addresses, financial identifiers, health identifiers). Do you classify and label them in logs?
- If Redwood stores prompt text for up to 30 days by default, can we get a write-once S3 export at 7 days and a guaranteed full purge after 30 days?
- For audit, can we get request-level metadata (request_id, model, time, region) for 365 days? We don't need raw text for that window, just the metadata.

Also — what level of access do Redwood engineers have to raw prompt/output text in hosted? Is there an internal ticketing process and access logs for any manual inspection?

If you prefer, we can have our security team send a short questionnaire next.

—Sara Jensen
Head of Platform Security, HelixAI
sara.jensen@helixai.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@helixai.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 09:08:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick asks on prompt/output PII retention

Sara — thanks, helpful list. Below are concrete answers mapped to your bullets; I also attached a one-page cheat sheet of PII categories we use internally.

1) PII classification:
- Our logging pipeline does not run a PII labeler by default on every prompt. We treat prompt/output text as potentially sensitive; the categories you listed (names, SSNs, phone, emails, financial, health identifiers) align with what we'd flag. We can enable an optional redaction/PII-detection step at ingest for Hosted customers on a per-account basis (requires configuration & has latency implications).

2) Exports & retention:
- We can provide a configurable export: scheduled S3 export (write-once) at your chosen cadence (7d is supported) for raw prompts/outputs.
- Default hosted retention windows (confirming): raw prompt/output payloads: 30 days; request traces/metadata: 90 days.
- Contract-level adjustments: via Dedicated or Private, we can reduce retention to customer-defined windows and enforce automated purge.

3) Access controls & engineer access: 
- Redwood engineers do not have bulk, unaudited access to raw prompt/output text. Access is gated by an internal request flow (support ticket with justification), approved by a manager, and logged. All manual inspections are recorded in an audit log with request_id and reviewer identity.

Next steps I propose: 
- I’ll share the internal one-pager (attached) and the export config example for S3.
- If HelixAI wants a formal security questionnaire, we’ll get our Security Engineering team to respond; we can also run a short PII redaction pilot on a sandbox key for you to validate latency impact.

Would you like me to route the questionnaire to legal@helixai.com or to secops directly?

Best,

Olga

Attachments: security-questionnaire-helixai.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@helixai.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 12:14:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick asks on prompt/output PII retention

Sara — quick note from pricing/ops: if HelixAI wants (a) scheduled 7-day S3 exports of raw prompts and (b) 365-day metadata retention, we can put that into the Dedicated contract as an add-on. Estimated incremental cost (ballpark) is $Xk/month for export and $Yk/month for extended storage and audit retention — I can get precise numbers once we have volume estimates (requests/month and average prompt size).

Olga — happy to hop on a short call with HelixAI secops next week to align on export format and S3 KMS keys.

-Markus
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@helixai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick asks on prompt/output PII retention

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Our legal team would prefer the security questionnaire first (looping legal@helixai.com) and a template S3 export config so we can validate key rotation and KMS policies. Can you send the questionnaire to legal@helixai.com and include an example S3 manifest?

We’re comfortable proceeding to a pilot if (1) the S3 export is write-once, (2) Redwood confirms purge at 30 days for hosted default and (3) engineer access is audited. If you can also include a sample redaction policy (optional step) so we can estimate latency impact, that would be ideal.

I’ll ask legal to create a short NDA-addendum for retention terms; once that’s in place we can move to a 30-day pilot key.

—Sara
Head of Platform Security, HelixAI
legal@helixai.com
